Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation; preserve the pinned benchmark and treat ablations as separate diagnostics ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Recommended protocol: persist the 200 validation users/category and seed-42 candidate pools, each containing the target once plus 99 unique negatives; reuse identical pools across original and perturbed histories. Keep repeated target occurrences in histories unless explicitly ablating them. Report prefix-only versus complete-training-history exclusion as separate diagnostic conditions, without changing host evaluation. Keep targets eligible in diagnostic ranking, explicitly documenting repeated-target exceptions. Use deterministic ordering by descending score then ascending item ID for diagnostics; preserve host tie handling for the official score.

For each user, measure paired HR@10 changes and top-k overlap, defined as intersection size divided by k. Predeclare perturbation types, strengths, repeat counts and seeds; reuse perturbations across models. Average perturbation repeats within user, then bootstrap users independently within each of the four datasets, preserving paired original/ablated observations. Compute each bootstrap replicate’s equally weighted dataset macro-average and report percentile intervals. These are proposed reproducibility controls, not a single established protocol. Keep sampled diagnostic overlap distinct from full-catalog simulator overlap.

For the simulator’s 20 users, encode each history once per perturbation, score every catalog item in chunks, mask complete training histories and padding, then merge chunk-local top-k results using the same deterministic ordering. RecBole documents split prediction and history masking ([implementation](https://www.recbole.io/docs/v1.1.1/_modules/recbole/trainer/trainer.html)). Cache item representations only while model weights remain fixed; key user-feature and recommendation caches by checkpoint, dataset, history, perturbation and exclusion policy. Streaming top-k avoids retaining the full score matrix. Preallocate diagnostic GPU time within the shared 43,200-second budget; bound perturbation repeats and full-catalog checkpoints without replacing required simulator recommendations with sampled candidates.
